SO1: The customer has licensed Sites Optimizer for AEM Sites (Edge Delivery, Cloud Service or Managed Services) and the site is a public production site. Hours scale with the number of sites.

How a fix is deployed depends on its opportunity. With the Ultimate package, approved content fixes go into authoring (on document-authored Edge Delivery sites, into the source documents) for people to review and publish, and Core Web Vitals fixes are prepared as code patches for a named developer who reviews, tests, merges and releases them. Deploying to authoring and preparing code patches each need the user's permission for that action and a fully configured site (Adobe's example is a connected code repository).

Code patches reach the developer as a pull request in the connected repository or as a downloaded patch; Adobe's October 2026 release notes list pull-request submission for Core Web Vitals as Early Access, so the route is confirmed here. On AEM as a Cloud Service sites, deploying broken-backlink redirects through Dispatcher is Early Access, used only where Adobe has enabled it.
With Prime, which identifies and suggests fixes, the first agreed content and configuration fixes are applied by hand and code fixes go to the named developer.
Core Web Vitals come from real-user data (Operational Telemetry, connected during setup if it isn't yet), and Adobe analyzes them only on pages with at least 1,000 page views.

Brand Visibility connects its own Search Console link; one access request to the customer covers both. Access for Adobe's scanner is confirmed here and its IP addresses are allowed in the CDN, firewall or Cloud Manager traffic filters.
SO2: Sites Optimizer is licensed and set up. Hours scale with the number of opportunities and sites. Sites Optimizer finds the opportunities and suggests fixes on its own.

How an approved fix is deployed depends on its opportunity: with the Ultimate package, content fixes go into authoring (on document-authored Edge Delivery sites, into the source documents) and people publish them, and Core Web Vitals fixes are prepared as code patches that the named developer reviews, tests, merges and releases through the existing development workflow.

Code patches arrive as pull requests or downloaded patches, by the route agreed at setup, and either way go through the customer's own review and release process; on AEM as a Cloud Service sites, broken-backlink redirects deploy through Dispatcher only where Adobe has enabled that Early Access feature.
With Prime (identify and suggest only), the partner applies approved content and configuration fixes by hand, and code fixes go to the named developer with Sites Optimizer's recommendation.

These hours cover reviewing and editing the suggestions with the content owner, deploying the content fixes, preparing the code patches and handing them to the developer, and the report; the developer's review, testing, merge and release are outside these hours unless agreed.

These are the month's site fixes in one allowance, and the site fixes Brand Visibility flags (robots.txt rules for AI crawlers, redirects for pages AI agents can't reach) are made by hand in the site's configuration or redirect sheet, within the same allowance.
F02: The customer has licensed Brand Concierge and supplies the approved content, current product facts, reviewers and the handoff destination; compliance decisions stay with the customer.

The documented handoff is live chat or meeting booking through Adobe Marketo Qualifier (formerly Sales Qualifier), which needs the representatives added as users in the Adobe Admin Console and at least one representative with a connected calendar (for meeting booking) or set live chat availability (for live chat); a handoff to another chat or contact-center platform is not a documented route and is confirmed with Adobe first.

Live chat and meeting booking don't need Marketo Engage: round robin and direct-agent routing work without it, and it is needed only for custom routing rules, which pick a team by Marketo attributes, and for writing concierge activities to the Marketo person record. Live chat conversations are kept for 30 days, so the customer confirms its own record-keeping needs.
The baseline is the anonymous, public-information experience; profile-based answers are not assumed. Hours scale with the number of products, sources, journeys and test conversations.

Adobe's Brand Concierge FAQ puts a basic setup at about 3 to 5 days, an advanced implementation at about 2 to 4 weeks and go-live at about 6 to 9 weeks. These hours are the partner's planning assumption for the work around that setup (approved sources and reviewers, conversation and disclosure design, the handoff, the golden-answer and refusal tests and the staged rollout) and are not yet reconciled with Adobe's figures or an independent delivery estimate.
